body:
@sestinj Proposed initial structure:
- Landing page (name, one line description, 3x on sentence descriptions about why to use Continue)
- Introduction (what is Continue, why to use it, how to get started)
- Getting started (steps to try out Continue using GitHub Codespaces with our best example)
- Installation (push everyone through using Continue packaged as a VS Code extension for now, via source)
- Walkthroughs (How to use GUI, How to use a recipe, How to create a recipe, How to share a recipe, etc)
- Concepts (explanations of all the key aspects: steps, recipes, GUI, SDK, etc)
- SDK (explanations of all of the methods, etc)
- Telemetry (we track anonymously, this is what we track, this is how you can opt out)

body:
Format 1: Sentence one, what we do. Sentence two, example.

Example: Airbnb is a marketplace where you can book a home or apartment when travelling for work or vacation. When you visit New York City with your family, instead of staying in a cramped and expensive hotel room, you can stay in a comfortable 3 bedroom apartment at the same price.

**Continue is an AI autopilot for coding which is fully open-source, making it easy for developers to write their own team/codebase-specific automations. For example, write tests or documentation that falls in line with team best practices.**

Format 2: Sentence one, the problem we solve. Sentence two, how we solve it.

Example: Stripe makes it easy for developers to accept payments on their websites or mobile apps. We do this by providing a simple and well documented payments API that any developer can instantly start using straight from our website.

**Continue makes it easy to extend AI coding tools so they can act directly in your IDE. We do this by providing a simple SDK where developers can write automations that are then usable in our VS Code extension.**
author: sestinj

body: @TyDunn I started using StarCoder yesterday and so wanted to group all llms/models under some namespace in the SDK. So it's now called `sdk.models.starcoder/gpt35/etc...`. So developers will primarily interact with the term "model." I've kept the `LLM` class because those are defined by capabilities, and nothing stops us from putting a different class in the models namespace. It would be misleading I think to name it anything else right now, because the capabilities are exactly that of a LLM, not more, and this is the most common naming convention (see https://github.com/jerryjliu/llama_index/tree/main, https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/Auto-GPT, https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain, https://github.com/getcursor/cursor)
author: sestinj

body: This is a good compromise. After your points yesterday, I started using `LLMs` all over the docs for now. We are far from a standardization here. OpenAI (calling GPT-4 a Large Multimodal Model) and Stanford (naming their research center CRFM), for example, will likely have more of a say in the ultimate name than many of those projects listed (though I agree let's align with them for now)
